verdict: No concrete oracle, source-byte, scalar, protocol-arithmetic or declared rejection expectation defect found within the bounded review.
method: Read CPU Rect contains/translated/intersect, Canvas image/blend and typed PushFixed/PopFixed paths; never executed them.
Manually derived each surviving half-open integer coverage rectangle and the fixed-scope restoration trace independently of the fixture expected LUTs.

Used an independent Python Fraction implementation of round-to-nearest-even binary32 after each subtract/divide/multiply; no native float arithmetic in finite rounding, no candidate imports or sampling helpers.
Compared all 642 independently calculated LUT entries and nine scalar cases, including signed intermediate infinities, to the proposed expectations.

Expanded hand-derived coverage/source-index arithmetic and the independently specified opaque 4x2 rectangle into mathematical color grids, then compared literal/direct-band grids and packed little-endian hashes. This is an oracle arithmetic check, not a renderer run.
Checked exact source RGBA bytes/palette dimensions/alpha/hash values, all 16 old evidence/source file bindings, and old protocol tuples via ast.literal_eval without importing the runner.
Read all negative/hidden/cap assembly definitions and checked integer budget arithmetic without constructing unbounded malformed data or submitting any plans.
Independently recomputed new protocol arithmetic from reviewer-derived coverage bounds, including one separately checked 4x2 opaque rectangle.

specific_derivations.translated_endpoint_tie: 2 + (1 + 2^-23) lies halfway between f32 3 and 3+2^-22. Even significand selects 3, so only x=2 survives. Width 1+2^-22 reaches 3+2^-22 and also covers integer x=3.
specific_derivations.subnormal: For m=2^-149, -m+2m=m, and ((0-(-m))/(2m))*2=1 exactly. The clipped positive width m covers integer 0, selecting B. Separately 1+m rounds to 1, yielding zero intersection width for the second image.
specific_derivations.fractional_clip: The tiny (.25,.25,.125,.125) draw includes integer (0,0) under frame clip, but the same draw under clip origin (.25,.25) loses that point. The larger clipped 1.5 square retains only (1,1), whose source index is (2,2), K.
specific_derivations.fixed_scope: Commands 3,5,7,9,14 have derived bounds [1,1,5,3], [4,2,5,3], [6,3,7,4], [4,2,5,3], [1,3,3,4]. Nested fixed escapes to caller clip; PopFixed restores the one-pixel fixed clip; final PopFixed/PopClip restore document offset and caller clip. Both K images remain hidden; H is later replaced by J.
specific_derivations.tail: 319x239 image writes only x<319,y<239. Source thresholds are integer x=160,y=120. Rounded 320x240 dispatch must preserve clear last row/column.
specific_derivations.clamp: Source width 1 clamps every scalar input to 0; finite tiny extent may produce +/-infinity during division, then clamps to final/first index. No visible-dispatch claim is inferred from scalar coordinates outside coverage.

protocol_review.storage_assumptions: Root-approved single packed source/LUT arena, 256-byte per-draw uniforms, output+readback eight bytes/pixel, no extra or dummy GPU buffer. If at least one image dispatch survives, all supplied source colors are packed once; with no surviving images, no image input buffer is created. CPU validation still covers all declared sources.

limitations: No engine, Canvas, candidate planner, compiler, build, adapter, Vulkan or GPU execution occurred. These are reviewed expectations, not observed GPU outputs or implementation conformance.
Binary32 arithmetic assumes round-to-nearest-even with gradual underflow as used by the specified CPU formula; integer-only GPU lookup avoids depending on shader float/subnormal semantics.
Negative cases were reviewed statically; no candidate rejection path or pre-device ordering was exercised. The 33-push negative also has an unclosed scope and is not an isolated depth diagnostic.
Positive buffer accounting relies on the explicitly approved storage layout and excludes CPU copies, transfer staging and native driver/device allocations.
143,360 LUT entries is a structural upper bound, not asserted independently reachable under all tighter limits. No full browser integration or performance claim is made.
